title: API
intro: Every address O2S calls, and the 2 public addresses it serves to van.com.pk: who may call each one, what goes in and out, the errors, and an example made from the code. O2S has no API versions.

items.title: Every address O2S calls or serves, at a glance

blocks.p: O2S is one web page (o2s.html) that talks to 1 server (server.js). All O2S data is 1 JSON document: the page reads it whole and writes it whole. The table lists every address the page calls, and the public addresses van.com.pk calls. Nothing else is called by O2S.

items.title: Sign in, the token, versions and limits (applies to every address)
src: server.js express.json limit and error handler (FIX C5)

head: Item
What the code does
rows: POST /api/login returns a token. The page keeps it in the browser (localStorage key van_token) and sends it on every call as the header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
Signed by the server (HMAC SHA-256 with SESSION_SECRET). It carries the username, the O2S role and the name, and lasts 30 days. No token, a bad one or an old one: 401 {"error":"unauthorized"}.

O2S reads the role from the token when it opens (decodeToken, restoreSession). A role changed on the server takes effect when that person signs in again. If you move your own role or change your own login on People, O2S signs you out (ppSave); a password reset or a name change of your own does not.

A login switched off on People and access gets 401 with 'This account has been switched off. Ask your platform administrator.' on every call, even with a valid token; sign in gives 403 with the same words, but only after the password is right (a wrong password still gives 401).
10 failures for one username in 15 minutes, then 429 until the 15 minutes pass. Kept in the server's memory, so a restart clears it.
JSON bodies up to 25 MB (express.json limit). Bigger: 413 {"error":"That is too large to upload here."}. A body that is not JSON: 400 {"error":"The request could not be read."}.

O2S does not version its API. There is no /v1 in any address and no version header. The page itself carries BUILD_ID; an open tab checks /o2s for a newer BUILD_ID and then refuses to save until refreshed.
No sign in. 60 lookups per visitor per 10 minutes (in memory), then 429. Browsers may call them only from https://van.com.pk and https://www.van.com.pk (plus PUBLIC_EXTRA_ORIGINS).

blocks.note: SESSION_SECRET: if it is not set, the server makes a temporary one and every login resets on restart. Whether it is set on Render is S-03 in the security register, not confirmed.

Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): the draft said any change to your own account signs you out. ppSave signs out only after a role move or a login rename; the old Edit person sheet (saveEditUser) signs out on any change, but nothing opens it now.

head: Part
Detail
rows: JSON {username, password}. The username is trimmed and made lower case.

401 'Incorrect username or password'; 429 'Too many failed sign-ins for this account. Try again in about N minutes, or ask your System Administrator to reset the password.'; 403 switched-off message; 500.
Saves the token, reads GET /api/state, lands everyone on Today (if the role can view it), writes 'Signed in' to the action log and saves.

blocks.p: Example, made from the code (not a real call): POST /api/login body {"username":"<login>","password":"..."} reply 200 {"token":"<payload>.<signature>","user":{"name":"<full name>","username":"<login>","role":"Supply Chain"}}

items.title: GET /api/state: read all O2S data
src: o2s.html bootState, doLogin, startSync, srvUpToDate, smpDispatch

head: Part
Detail
rows: Any signed-in login. The server does not check the O2S role (security register S-01).
None. Header Authorization: Bearer <token>. O2S asks with cache: no-store, except smpDispatch, which sends no cache setting.
{rev, data}. rev is a whole number that goes up by 1 on every save. data is the whole O2S document (orders, shipments, batches, packingLog, masters and the rest) with the users list taken out.

On opening and after sign in; when /api/rev shows a new rev; before a decision that must be taken on the latest records (srvUpToDate, 8 second time limit); before issuing a sample gate pass number (smpDispatch).
rev 0 and data null: O2S builds the starting data (buildFromSeed) and saves it. Data without orders: O2S refuses to overwrite and retries every 4 seconds.

blocks.p: Example, made from the code (not a real call): GET /api/state reply 200 {"rev":4812,"data":{"orders":[...],"shipments":[...],"batches":[...],"masters":{...}}}

blocks.note: Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): smpDispatch reads GET /api/state with the sign-in header only and no cache setting; every other GET /api/state call asks for no-store.

items.title: POST /api/state: save all O2S data, with the x-base-rev check and 409

head: Part
Detail
rows: Any signed-in login (S-01: no O2S role check on the server).
The whole O2S document as JSON (dataOnly: without currentUser, role, screen, expanded, users). Header X-Base-Rev: the rev this copy was loaded at.
Someone saved after this copy was loaded. Reply 409 {conflict:true, rev, data}: the server's current copy. Nothing is written.
The server writes with no check. O2S always sends the header.
401 (O2S signs the person out); 413 over 25 MB; 500.
400 ms after the last change (save, then saveNow). Not while a newer build is waiting: the toast says refresh to save.

steps.text: A change is made; save waits 400 ms, then sends the whole document with X-Base-Rev
Does the rev still match? yes: write, rev + 1, reply 200 {rev}; no: reply 409 with the server copy
On 409: merge 3 ways (the copy loaded, this copy, the server copy), keep both people's changes, warn if one DC or gate pass number went to 2 trucks
Send the merged copy again (up to 5 tries, then again every 3 seconds, never stops with the change unsent)

blocks.p: Example, made from the code (not a real call): POST /api/state header X-Base-Rev: 4812, body {"orders":[...],...} reply 200 {"rev":4813}; or reply 409 {"conflict":true,"rev":4814,"data":{...}}

blocks.note: Known limit: audit rows without an id can be lost in the merge when 2 people save at once (S-09). DC and gate pass numbers are taken as highest + 1 in each copy, so a clash is possible; O2S says so after the merge (mergeDupNumbers).

head: Part
Detail
rows: Every 7 seconds, but not when the tab is hidden, while typing in a box, while a sheet is open, while an entry is unsaved, or while a save is waiting. A new rev makes O2S read GET /api/state and merge.

blocks.p: Example, made from the code (not a real call): GET /api/rev reply 200 {"rev":4813}

items.title: GET /api/me: on the server, not used by O2S

blocks.p: Returns {username, name, title, o2sRole, platformAdmin, modules, adminModules} for the signed-in login. It drives the launcher tiles. O2S takes its role from the token instead and never calls this address.

items.title: GET /o2s: the page itself, and the newer-build check

blocks.p: Any address that no other route claims (and that does not start with /api) is answered with o2s.html, sent with no-store. An open O2S tab fetches /o2s at most once every 10 minutes, reads only the first 4,000 characters, and compares BUILD_ID. If it differs, a banner asks for a refresh and saving is blocked until the page is refreshed.
Example, made from the code (not a real call): GET /o2s reply 200 text/html, starting with ... BUILD_ID='2026-10-16a' ...

blocks.note: Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): the example BUILD_ID was 2026-10-15g; the file read tonight carries 2026-10-16a.

items.title: GET /api/public/batch/:batch: is there an approved lab report for this bag?
src: apps/o2s/public-routes.js header (Tahir's rulings 3 Oct 2026), find, buildIndex, headers

head: Part
Detail
rows: Anyone, no sign in. Read only: nothing here writes O2S data.
The batch number printed on the bag. Trimmed, upper case, spaces removed; must be 3 to 20 letters, digits or hyphens. Internal production and lot numbers are never accepted.
Empty body: no such printed number, or not every lot behind it has an approved COA, or the number is not valid.
Empty body: more than 60 lookups from one visitor in 10 minutes.
Empty body; the reason goes to the server log only.
A number used in 2 financial years (July to June) answers with the newest year. Reversed or void packing runs are left out. The index is rebuilt only when the O2S rev changes.
Cache-Control no-store; X-Robots-Tag noindex; Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for van.com.pk and www.van.com.pk.

blocks.p: Example, made from the code (not a real call): GET /api/public/batch/VAN6JE001 reply 200 {"batch":"VAN6JE001","approved_on":"2026-09-20","report_url":"https://.../api/public/batch/VAN6JE001/report.pdf"}

items.title: GET /api/public/batch/:batch/report.pdf: the lab report as a PDF
src: apps/o2s/public-routes.js writeReport, drawCoa, publicCoa, summaryCoa, layoutOf

head: Part
Detail
rows: Anyone, no sign in. Same checks, limits and 404 rules as API-13.

application/pdf, form QCL-FRM-12.03 Quality Analysis Report, A4. Opens and prints; copying, editing and text extraction are refused (random owner password per download); watermark and download stamp on every page.

Batch No. (the printed number), Mfg and Exp date, test details, issue date and revision, the 6 table columns with Remarks and Overall, the disclaimer, signature roles and dates, and the approver's name only when O2S holds a person's name.
Item name, source, Q.C. No., quantity, who received the sample, the analyst's and reviewer's names, the deviation line, internal numbers.

REPORT_LAYOUT=summary (default): 1 report, the first FIT lot in production order (the first lot when none is FIT), marked 'Results of production lot i of n of this batch'. A number with only 1 lot gets that lot's report with no such line. REPORT_LAYOUT=per-lot: 1 page per lot.

blocks.p: Example, made from the code (not a real call): GET /api/public/batch/VAN6JE001/report.pdf reply 200 Content-Type application/pdf, Content-Disposition inline; filename="VAN-VAN6JE001-quality-analysis-report.pdf"

blocks.note: Several lots behind 1 number is marked UNDER DISCUSSION in the file header; summary is the default until Tahir rules.
Corrected 16 Oct 2026 (independent check against the code): summaryCoa takes the first lot when no lot is FIT, and writeReport uses the single lot as it is when there is only 1 (no lot line).

list: /api/platform/catalogue, users, access (POST, DELETE), admin, people/:username (PATCH), people/:username/password, people/:username/active, people/:username/history, holders: the launcher's People and access
/robots.txt, /assets, /, /launcher, /drop, /pd, /nigehbaan: pages and files of other apps

blocks.p: A role can also be given or taken away from the launcher (POST or DELETE /api/platform/access). It writes the same O2S role column O2S reads, so O2S sees it at the person's next sign in.
All need sign in (the same token as every O2S call), except the 3 files. Until the 3 keys are set on the server and the 3 tables exist, every address answers "not ready" and nothing is sent.

head: Address
Who
What it does
rows: The part of O2S that receives alerts while O2S is closed, the app name and the icons for the Home Screen.
Ready or not, and the public key a device needs to switch on.
Switches alerts on for this browser, for the person signed in. 1 browser = 1 row; whoever switches on last owns it. Only an address of the push services of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari is taken.
Switches this browser off (own device only). Sign out calls it.
Is this browser on for me? If another login switched it on, it is switched off for that login.
Sends a test alert to my own devices.
Every person with an O2S role (switched-off logins left out) and their devices with alerts on.

The Today jobs a screen sees: mode save (new after a save) or sweep (the 15-minute list). The server checks the job name against its roles, the escalation target, decides who gets it, and sends. At most 30 calls a minute per login, 2,000 jobs per 15-minute list and 100 per save; a sweep at most once per 10 minutes and only from a screen up to date with the server.

blocks.note: Every alert address answers {ok:false} on an error instead of stopping the server (Express 4 does not catch errors in async routes).
